title: My Calendar III
prompt: A k-booking happens when k events all have some non-empty intersection at a common moment. Design a `MyCalendarThree` class that, given events represented by half-open intervals `[start, end)`, supports `book(start, end)` which adds the event and returns an integer representing the maximum k-booking currently achieved by any moment in the calendar, i.e. the maximum number of events that overlap at any single point in time after this booking is added.

examples.explanation: After book(5,15), the point 10 is covered by [10,20), [10,40), and [5,15) — a triple booking, so the running maximum k becomes 3.
A single booking on an empty calendar always yields a k-booking of exactly 1.
Touching half-open intervals ([1,5) and [5,10)) share no common instant, so they never combine into a higher k-booking.

constraints: at most 400 calls will be made to book
hints: Think of this as a sweep-line problem: each booking is a +1 event at `start` and a -1 event at `end`. The maximum k-booking overall is the maximum running sum at any point across all events seen so far.
You don't need a segment tree for this constraint size — a sorted map (or dictionary plus sorted keys) from position to delta works, since you re-sweep from scratch on every call.
After adding the new +1/-1 deltas, sort all keys and sweep left to right accumulating the running sum, tracking its maximum. This max is the answer to return for this call.

solution.approach: Model every booking as two delta events: +1 at `start` and -1 at `end`, stored in a dictionary keyed by position. After adding the new event's deltas, sweep through all keys in sorted order, accumulating a running sum (the number of events active at that position) and tracking the maximum value reached. This maximum is exactly the highest k-booking achieved anywhere on the timeline, since the running sum after processing all deltas up to and including a given position equals the count of active events at that instant. Given the small call limit (at most 400), re-sweeping all events on every call is efficient enough; a segment tree with coordinate compression or lazy propagation would be used for much larger constraints.
solution.code:
from collections import defaultdict


def my_calendar_three(operations, args):
    delta = defaultdict(int)
    results = []

    for op, arg in zip(operations, args):
        if op != 'book':
            continue
        start, end = arg[0], arg[1]
        delta[start] += 1
        delta[end] -= 1

        running = 0
        best = 0
        for pos in sorted(delta.keys()):
            running += delta[pos]
            best = max(best, running)
        results.append(best)

    return results
solution.timeComplexity: O(n^2 log n) overall for n calls (each call re-sorts up to n keys)
